limits: microphone is what the audio side last reported; with no engine in this build it stays `unknown` and that is not the same as `not_determined`

speech is macOS's own answer (SFSpeechRecognizer.authorizationStatus), read when this is asked while the daemon has an audio engine, whose Apple recogniser is what needs it; a read never asks for the grant. With no engine it is what the audio side last reported, `unknown` like the microphone

bluetooth is CoreBluetooth's authorization for this process as the BLE voice link last read it (`[voice] transport = "ble"`, where the deck's microphone and speaker need it instead of Microphone); `unknown` on the CoreAudio transport and until the link has started. macOS asks for it by itself the first time the link starts, so there is no `perm.request` for it, and a denial is lifted in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Bluetooth

accessibility is what the Macropad keys last learned by trying: `granted` once a keystroke went out, `denied` after macOS refused one (which also puts the system prompt up, once per run), and `unknown` until a key has been pressed or `perm.request` asked

a grant reported here is this process's. A launchd-spawned deckd is its own responsible process with its own TCC row, so a status read from a terminal-spawned daemon says nothing about the shipped one (W4 V9)
